content: 1. Pyrimethamine's mechanism of action involves pharmacodynamic synergism. It may lead to increased bone marrow toxicity, and close monitoring is advised. 2. Quinidine increases the level or effect of sulfamethoxazole by competing for renal tubular clearance as a basic (cationic) drug. This interaction is significant and alternative drugs should be considered due to the risk of QTc interval prolongation when both drugs are used together. 3. Sulfamethoxazole increases the level or effect of quinine through basic drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 4. Sulfamethoxazole increases the level or effect of ramelteon by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 5. Sulfamethoxazole and ranolazine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 6. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of repaglinide by competing for plasma protein binding. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 7. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of sulfamethoxazole by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Rifapentine decreases the level or effect of sulfamethoxazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 9. Sulfamethoxazole and risperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 10. Non-aspirin salicylates increase the levels of sulfamethoxazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 11. Salsalate increases the levels of sulfamethoxazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Selegiline transdermal increases the levels of sulfamethoxazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 13. Sulfamethoxazole increases the level or effect of siponimod by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Co-administration with drugs that moderately inhibit CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 is not recommended. Caution is advised when siponimod is co-administered with moderate CYP2C9 inhibitors alone. 14. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of sodium picosulfate by altering colonic bacterial flora required for its activation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 15. Sulfamethoxazole and sotalol both prolong the QTc interval. Alternative drugs should be considered. 16. Spironolactone increases the levels of sulfamethoxazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Sulfasalazine increases the levels of sulfamethoxazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 18. Sulfamethoxazole affects tamoxifen metabolism by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10, reducing the formation of active metabolites. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 19. Sulfamethoxazole and telavancin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 20. Sulfamethoxazole increases the level or effect of terbinafine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 21. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the level or effect of thiamine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 22. Thioridazine and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 23. Ticlopidine increases the level or effect of sulfamethoxazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 24. Torsemide increases the levels of sulfamethoxazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 25. Tranylcypromine increases the levels of sulfamethoxazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Trazodone and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole decreases trazodone levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 27. Sulfamethoxazole and tretinoin increase phototoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 28. Sulfamethoxazole and topical tretinoin increase phototoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 29. Sulfamethoxazole increases the level or effect of triamterene by competing for renal tubular clearance as a basic (cationic) drug. Triamterene increases the levels of sulfamethoxazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 30. Trifluoperazine and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 31. Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole increases the level or effect of trimethoprim by competing for renal tubular clearance as a basic (cationic) drug. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 32. Trimipramine and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole decreases trimipramine levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 33. Sulfamethoxazole and tropisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 34. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the effects of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is complete. 35. Valganciclovir increases the toxicity of sulfamethoxazole through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 36. Sulfamethoxazole and valoctocogene roxaparvovec may both increase hepatotoxicity. Medications with potential hepatotoxic effects should be closely monitored, and alternative drugs should be considered. 37. Valproic acid increases the level or effect of sulfamethoxazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 38. Sulfamethoxazole and venlafaxine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 39. Sulfamethoxazole increases the level or effect of verapamil by competing for renal tubular clearance as a basic (cationic) drug. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 40. Sulfamethoxazole and verteporfin increase phototoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 41. Sulfamethoxazole and voriconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole increases the level or effect of voriconazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism, and vice versa. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 42. Sulfamethoxazole increases the level or effect of warfarin by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9 and displacing protein binding. If co-administered, consider reducing the warfarin dose by 10-20%. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 43. Willow bark increases the levels of sulfamethoxazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 44. Zafirlukast increases the level or effect of sulfamethoxazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 45. Zidovudine increases the toxicity of sulfamethoxazole through pharmacodynamic synergism. Sulfamethoxazole increases zidovudine levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 46. Sulfamethoxazole and ziprasidone both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended.
